source_text: וַ/יֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֖/י מִי אָ֑תָּה ו/יאמר אֵלָ֔י/ו עֲמָלֵקִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי־׃
english_snapshot: He said to me[a], ‘Who are you?’ And I said to him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’

signals.text: Hebrew has 'and he said' in the second clause; in context the sense is 'and I said,' since the speaker is recounting his own reply to Saul.

source_text: בֶּן אַרְבָּעִ֨ים שָׁנָ֜ה אִֽישׁ בֹּ֣שֶׁת בֶּן שָׁא֗וּל בְּ/מָלְכ/וֹ֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּ/שְׁתַּ֥יִם שָׁנִ֖ים מָלָ֑ךְ אַ֚ךְ בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה הָי֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י דָוִֽד־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel[a], and he reigned two years[c][b]. But the house of Judah followed David.

signals.text: The name appears here in the Masoretic Text as Ish-bosheth; compare the alternative form Eshbaal in related traditions.

source_text: וַ/יֵּ֨לֶךְ הַ/מֶּ֤לֶךְ וַֽ/אֲנָשָׁי/ו֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֶל הַ/יְבֻסִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָ/אָ֑רֶץ וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר לְ/דָוִ֤ד לֵ/אמֹר֙ לֹא תָב֣וֹא הֵ֔נָּה כִּ֣י אִם הֱסִֽירְ/ךָ֗ הַ/עִוְרִ֤ים וְ/הַ/פִּסְחִים֙ לֵ/אמֹ֔ר לֹֽא יָב֥וֹא דָוִ֖ד הֵֽנָּה־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem[a], to the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land. And they said to David, “You will not come in here, for even the blind and the lame will turn you away,” saying[b], “David will not come in here.”

signals.text: Or, following the Hebrew singular, 'and he said to David'; the singular likely functions collectively for the Jebusite inhabitants.

source_text: וַ/יַּ֤עַשׂ דָּוִד֙ כֵּ֔ן כַּ/אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖/הוּ יְהוָ֑ה וַ/יַּךְ֙ אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מִ/גֶּ֖בַע עַד בֹּאֲ/ךָ֥ גָֽזֶר־־׃פ
english_snapshot: And David did so[a], just as Yahweh had commanded him[b], and he struck down the Philistines from Geba as far as Gezer.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'from Geba.' Some translations differ here due to textual or parallel-passage considerations.

source_text: בְּ/כֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי֮ בְּ/כָל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ הֲ/דָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת אַחַד֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֗יתִי לִ/רְע֛וֹת אֶת עַמִּ֥/י אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵ/אמֹ֑ר לָ֛/מָּה לֹֽא בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖/י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: In all the places where I have walked among all the sons of Israel[a], did I ever speak a word to one of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’

signals.text: Hebrew: 'one of the tribes of Israel'; the parallel in 1 Chronicles 17:6 reads 'judges of Israel,' which likely reflects the leaders charged to shepherd the people.

source_text: וְ/נֶאְמַ֨ן בֵּיתְ/ךָ֧ וּ/מַֽמְלַכְתְּ/ךָ֛ עַד עוֹלָ֖ם לְ/פָנֶ֑י/ךָ כִּֽסְאֲ/ךָ֔ יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֖וֹן עַד עוֹלָֽם־־׃
english_snapshot: And your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me[b][a]; your throne shall be established forever.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'before you'; some textual witnesses read 'before me.'

source_text: וַ/יַּ֣ךְ דָּוִ֔ד אֶת הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר בֶּן רְחֹ֖ב מֶ֣לֶךְ צוֹבָ֑ה בְּ/לֶכְתּ֕/וֹ לְ/הָשִׁ֥יב יָד֖/וֹ בִּֽ/נְהַר־־־׃
english_snapshot: David struck down Hadadezer son of Rehob[a], king of Zobah[c][b], when he went to restore his power at the River.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Hadadezer'; some textual traditions and the parallel in 1 Chronicles read 'Hadarezer.'

source_text: וַ/יִּלְכֹּ֨ד דָּוִ֜ד מִמֶּ֗/נּוּ אֶ֤לֶף וּ/שְׁבַע מֵאוֹת֙ פָּרָשִׁ֔ים וְ/עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ רַגְלִ֑י וַ/יְעַקֵּ֤ר דָּוִד֙ אֶת כָּל הָ/רֶ֔כֶב וַ/יּוֹתֵ֥ר מִמֶּ֖/נּוּ מֵ֥אָה רָֽכֶב־־־׃
english_snapshot: David captured from him 1,700 horsemen and 20,000 foot soldiers[a]. Then David hamstrung all the chariot horses[c][b], but left enough for 100 chariots.

signals.text: The Hebrew text reads '1,700 horsemen.' The parallel in 1 Chronicles 18:4 reads '7,000 horsemen.'

source_text: מֵ/אֲרָ֤ם וּ/מִ/מּוֹאָב֙ וּ/מִ/בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וּ/מִ/פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וּ/מֵֽ/עֲמָלֵ֑ק וּ/מִ/שְּׁלַ֛ל הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר בֶּן רְחֹ֖ב מֶ֥לֶךְ צוֹבָֽה־׃
english_snapshot: from Aram[a], and from Moab, and from the Ammonites, and from the Philistines, and from Amalek, and from the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob[c][b], king of Zobah.

signals.text: Some passages spell the name 'Hadarezer.'

source_text: וַ/יַּ֤עַשׂ דָּוִד֙ שֵׁ֔ם בְּ/שֻׁב֕/וֹ מֵ/הַכּוֹת֥/וֹ אֶת אֲרָ֖ם בְּ/גֵיא מֶ֑לַח שְׁמוֹנָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אָֽלֶף־־׃
english_snapshot: And David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down Aram in the Valley of Salt—eighteen thousand men[a].

signals.text: Some witnesses and the parallel in 1 Chronicles 18:12 point to 'Edom' rather than 'Aram.'

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל הַ/מֶּ֔לֶךְ כְּ/כֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצַוֶּ֜ה אֲדֹנִ֤/י הַ/מֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת עַבְדּ֔/וֹ כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑/ךָ וּ/מְפִיבֹ֗שֶׁת אֹכֵל֙ עַל שֻׁלְחָנִ֔/י כְּ/אַחַ֖ד מִ/בְּנֵ֥י הַ/מֶּֽלֶךְ־־־׃
english_snapshot: Ziba said to the king[a], “According to all that my lord the king commands his servant[b], so your servant will do.” And Mephibosheth ate at my table like one of the king’s sons.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'my table.' Some translations render 'the king’s table' to smooth the shift in person, but the Masoretic Text preserves the first person, likely reflecting David’s perspective.

source_text: וַ/יָּ֣נָס אֲרָם֮ מִ/פְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַ/יַּהֲרֹ֨ג דָּוִ֜ד מֵ/אֲרָ֗ם שְׁבַ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֔כֶב וְ/אַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְ/אֵ֨ת שׁוֹבַ֧ךְ שַׂר צְבָא֛/וֹ הִכָּ֖ה וַ/יָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם־׃
english_snapshot: Aram fled from before Israel[a], and David killed seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand horsemen from Aram. He also struck down Shobach, the commander of their army[b], and he died there.

signals.text: Hebrew 'seven hundred chariot/chariotry.' The exact referent may be the chariot force, hence 'charioteers.' 1 Chronicles 19:18 has 'seven thousand chariots.'

source_text: אוּלַ֛י יִרְאֶ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה ב/עונ/י וְ/הֵשִׁ֨יב יְהוָ֥ה לִ/י֙ טוֹבָ֔ה תַּ֥חַת קִלְלָת֖/וֹ הַ/יּ֥וֹם הַ/זֶּֽה׃
english_snapshot: Perhaps Yahweh will look on my affliction[a], and Yahweh will repay me with good in place of his cursing this day.

signals.text: Or, following the written form, 'my iniquity.'

source_text: וְ/אֶת עֲמָשָׂ֗א שָׂ֧ם אַבְשָׁלֹ֛ם תַּ֥חַת יוֹאָ֖ב עַל הַ/צָּבָ֑א וַ/עֲמָשָׂ֣א בֶן אִ֗ישׁ וּ/שְׁמ/וֹ֙ יִתְרָ֣א הַ/יִּשְׂרְאֵלִ֔י אֲשֶׁר בָּא֙ אֶל אֲבִיגַ֣ל בַּת נָחָ֔שׁ אֲח֥וֹת צְרוּיָ֖ה אֵ֥ם יוֹאָֽב־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And Absalom set Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Ithra the Israelite[a], who had gone in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Ithra the Israelite.' 1 Chronicles 2:17 has 'Jether the Ishmaelite.'

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֤אמֶר הָ/אִישׁ֙ אֶל יוֹאָ֔ב ו/לא אָנֹכִ֜י שֹׁקֵ֤ל עַל כַּפַּ/י֙ אֶ֣לֶף כֶּ֔סֶף לֹֽא אֶשְׁלַ֥ח יָדִ֖/י אֶל בֶּן הַ/מֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י בְ/אָזְנֵ֜י/נוּ צִוָּ֣ה הַ/מֶּ֗לֶךְ אֹ֠תְ/ךָ וְ/אֶת אֲבִישַׁ֤י וְ/אֶת אִתַּי֙ לֵ/אמֹ֔ר שִׁמְרוּ מִ֕י בַּ/נַּ֖עַר בְּ/אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם־־־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: But the man said to Joab[a], “Even if I were weighing out a thousand pieces of silver on my palms, I would not put out my hand against the king’s son; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying[b], ‘Guard for me the young man Absalom.’”

signals.text: The Hebrew text at the end of the verse is difficult: literally, 'Guard מי the young man, Absalom.' Many understand the sense from 18:5 as 'Guard for me the young man Absalom.'

source_text: וַֽ/יַּעֲבֹ֞ר בְּ/כָל שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָבֵ֛לָ/ה וּ/בֵ֥ית מַעֲכָ֖ה וְ/כָל הַ/בֵּרִ֑ים ו/יקלהו וַ/יָּבֹ֖אוּ אַף אַחֲרָֽי/ו־־ס־׃
english_snapshot: He passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth-maacah[b][a], and all the Berites assembled and also followed after him.

signals.text: Hebrew 'all the Berites.' Some translations read 'all the Bichrites,' connecting the phrase to Sheba son of Bichri from the context; the Masoretic Text here more directly supports 'Berites.'

source_text: וַ/יִּקַּ֣ח הַ/מֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת שְׁ֠נֵי בְּנֵ֨י רִצְפָּ֤ה בַת אַיָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָלְדָ֣ה לְ/שָׁא֔וּל אֶת אַרְמֹנִ֖י וְ/אֶת מְפִבֹ֑שֶׁת וְ/אֶת חֲמֵ֗שֶׁת בְּנֵי֙ מִיכַ֣ל בַּת שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלְדָ֛ה לְ/עַדְרִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן בַּרְזִלַּ֖י הַ/מְּחֹלָתִֽי־־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: So the king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah[a], whom she had borne to Saul—Armoni and Mephibosheth—and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and ancient interpreters have 'Merab' instead of 'Michal'; compare 1 Samuel 18:19, where Adriel is said to have married Merab, Saul's daughter.

source_text: ו/ישבו בְּנֹ֜ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּ/ילִידֵ֣י הָ/רָפָ֗ה וּ/מִשְׁקַ֤ל קֵינ/וֹ֙ שְׁלֹ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וְ/ה֖וּא חָג֣וּר חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וַ/יֹּ֖אמֶר לְ/הַכּ֥וֹת אֶת דָּוִֽד׀־׃
english_snapshot: And Ishbi-benob[a], who was among the descendants of Rapha, whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of bronze, and who was girded with a new sword[c][b], said that he would strike down David.

signals.text: The Hebrew name form is uncertain; 'Ishbi-benob' follows the traditional understanding. Possible alternatives include 'Jesbi-benob' or a different division of the consonants.

source_text: וַֽ/יְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַ/תְּהִי ע֧וֹד הַ/מִּלְחָמָ֛ה בְּ/ג֖וֹב עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים אָ֣ז הִכָּ֗ה סִבְּכַי֙ הַ/חֻ֣שָׁתִ֔י אֶת סַ֕ף אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּ/ילִדֵ֥י הָ/רָפָֽה־־־־׃פ
english_snapshot: After this[a], there was again war with the Philistines at Gob, and then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph[b], who was among the descendants of Rapha.

signals.text: Hebrew 'Saph'; the parallel in 1 Chronicles 20:4 has the name 'Sippai.'

source_text: וַ/תְּהִי ע֧וֹד הַ/מִּלְחָמָ֛ה בְּ/ג֖וֹב עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַ/יַּ֡ךְ אֶלְחָנָן֩ בֶּן יַעְרֵ֨י אֹרְגִ֜ים בֵּ֣ית הַלַּחְמִ֗י אֵ֚ת גָּלְיָ֣ת הַ/גִּתִּ֔י וְ/עֵ֣ץ חֲנִית֔/וֹ כִּ/מְנ֖וֹר אֹרְגִֽים־־־׃ס
english_snapshot: And there was again war at Gob with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim[a] the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite[b], and the shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam.

signals.text: The Hebrew patronymic 'Jaare-oregim' is difficult; some think 'oregim' ('weavers') was accidentally repeated from the end of the verse.

The Masoretic Samuel text and the Greek comparison text name Goliath as Elhanan's opponent. The parallel in 1 Chronicles 20:5 instead names Lahmi, the brother of Goliath; it is a parallel account, not another manuscript of this Samuel verse. The fragmentary 1QSam (1Q7) material sometimes indexed here does not securely preserve the disputed names and cannot settle the difference.

source_text: וַ/יְחָרֵ֖ף אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַ/יַּכֵּ֨/הוּ֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן בֶּן שמעי אֲחִ֥י דָוִֽד־־׃
english_snapshot: And he defied Israel[a], and Jonathan the son of Shimei, David’s brother, struck him down.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and the parallel in 1 Chronicles 20:7 read 'Shimea' or 'Shimeah' instead of 'Shimei.'

source_text: אֵ֛לֶּה שְׁמ֥וֹת הַ/גִּבֹּרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְ/דָוִ֑ד יֹשֵׁ֨ב בַּשֶּׁ֜בֶת תַּחְכְּמֹנִ֣י רֹ֣אשׁ הַ/שָּׁלִשִׁ֗י ה֚וּא עֲדִינ֣/וֹ ה/עצנ/ו עַל שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֛וֹת חָלָ֖ל בְּ/פַ֥עַם אחד׀־׃ס
english_snapshot: These are the names of the mighty men who belonged to David: Josheb-basshebeth[a], a Tahkemonite, chief of the Three. He was Adino the Eznite[c][b], who wielded his spear against eight hundred slain at one time.

signals.text: The Hebrew text of this verse is difficult. 'Josheb-basshebeth' follows the Masoretic Text; the parallel in 1 Chronicles 11:11 reads 'Jashobeam, a Hachmonite.'
Or 'chief of the thirty,' according to some ancient witnesses and interpreters; the Masoretic Text reads 'chief of the Three.'

source_text: וַ/אֲבִישַׁ֞י אֲחִ֣י יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֗ה ה֚וּא רֹ֣אשׁ ה/שלשי וְ/הוּא֙ עוֹרֵ֣ר אֶת חֲנִית֔/וֹ עַל שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת חָלָ֑ל וְ/ל/וֹ שֵׁ֖ם בַּ/שְּׁלֹשָֽׁה׀־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Abishai[a], the brother of Joab son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against three hundred and killed them[b], and he had a name among the Three.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'chief of the Three.' Some interpreters, influenced by the parallel in 1 Chronicles 11:20 and textual uncertainty in this section, understand the group as 'the Thirty' instead.

source_text: אֵ֣לֶּה עָשָׂ֔ה בְּנָיָ֖הוּ בֶּן יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע וְ/ל/וֹ שֵׁ֖ם בִּ/שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה הַ/גִּבֹּרִֽים־־׃
english_snapshot: These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did[b][a], and he had a name among the three mighty men.

signals.text: Some interpreters understand this in light of the larger list of David's warriors and compare readings involving 'the thirty'; the Hebrew text here reads 'the three.'

source_text: אֲבִֽי עַלְבוֹן֙ הָֽ/עַרְבָתִ֔י עַזְמָ֖וֶת הַ/בַּרְחֻמִֽי־׃ס
english_snapshot: Abi-albon the Arbathite[a], Azmaveth the Barhumite[b];

signals.text: 'Barhumite' follows the Masoretic Text; some relate the designation to Bahurim and render 'Baharumite.'

source_text: אֶלְיַחְבָּא֙ הַ/שַּׁ֣עַלְבֹנִ֔י בְּנֵ֥י יָשֵׁ֖ן יְהוֹנָתָֽן׃ס
english_snapshot: Elyahba the Shaalbonite[a], the sons of Jashen, Jonathan.

signals.text: The Hebrew text is terse and difficult here: literally, 'Elyahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan.' Some interpreters understand a textual irregularity and reconstruct the list differently, such as taking 'Jonathan' as one of 'the sons of Jashen.' This translation preserves the Hebrew wording as transmitted rather than emending it.

source_text: וַ/יָּבֹא גָ֥ד אֶל דָּוִ֖ד וַ/יַּגֶּד ל֑/וֹ וַ/יֹּ֣אמֶר ל֡/וֹ הֲ/תָב֣וֹא לְ/ךָ֣ שֶֽׁבַע שָׁנִ֣ים רָעָ֣ב בְּ/אַרְצֶ֡/ךָ אִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳ֠דָשִׁים נֻסְ/ךָ֨ לִ/פְנֵֽי צָרֶ֜י/ךָ וְ/ה֣וּא רֹדְפֶ֗/ךָ וְ/אִם הֱ֠יוֹת שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֥ים דֶּ֨בֶר֙ בְּ/אַרְצֶ֔/ךָ עַתָּה֙ דַּ֣ע וּ/רְאֵ֔ה מָה אָשִׁ֥יב שֹׁלְחִ֖/י דָּבָֽר־־־׀׀־־־־׃ס
english_snapshot: So Gad came to David and told him[a], and said to him[c][b], “Shall seven years of famine come to you in your land? Or will you flee three months before your adversaries while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of pestilence in your land? Now know and see what answer I should return to the one who sent me.”

signals.text: The parallel in 1 Chronicles 21:12 reads 'three years of famine' instead of 'seven years.'
